subtitle: From Forest Trail to Coin and Crown

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle close on a weathered Roman denarius held in a calloused hand, Deccan forest and distant hill of Chandravalli blurred behind
panels.action: Chandravalli Trader stands in a shadowed Deccan grove, holding up a gleaming Roman silver coin as mist curls around the Chandravalli hill behind him and an ancient path snakes into the forest.

dialogue.text: In a Deccan forest hollow, a Roman coin, a Han token and a Kadamba name meet, revealing how Banavasi’s rulers inherited an older world of roads, markets and power.

i18n.hi: दक्कन के गह्वर में रोमन सिक्का, हान टोकन और कदंब नाम मिलते हैं, दिखाते हैं कि बनवासी के शासकों ने पुरानी राहों, बाज़ारों और सत्ता की दुनिया विरासत में पाई।

panels.shot: wide bird’s-eye over the bowl-shaped valley of Chandravalli, ringed by low hills and forest, with a shimmering tank at the centre
panels.action: From above, the Chandravalli basin lies like a shallow bowl, its central tank reflecting the sky as footpaths, huts and scattered stone cairns dot the valley floor and wooded ridges rise around.

dialogue.text: Chandravalli, near Chitradurga—today a quiet hollow of trees and rock—was once a crossroads where forest paths, caravans and kings’ ambitions crossed the Deccan sky.

i18n.hi: चित्रदुर्ग के पास चंद्रवल्ली—आज पेड़ों‑चट्टानों की खामोश घाटी—कभी वह मोड़ थी जहाँ जंगल‑पथ, काफिले और राजाओं की野सियाँ दक्कन के आसमान पर टकराती थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level of Chandravalli Trader as a generic early 20th-century excavator, kneeling by a trench amid boulders and scrub
panels.action: Chandravalli Trader, dressed as an early archaeologist, kneels by a freshly cut trench at the base of a rocky slope, brush in hand, while labourers in the background lift baskets of earth from a stepped pit.

dialogue.text: Two thousand years later, men like R. Narasimhachar, M. H. Krishna and Mortimer Wheeler sliced trenches into this earth, reading its layers like pages of a long-buried record.

i18n.hi: दो हज़ार साल बाद, आर. नरसिंहाचार, एम. एच. कृष्ण और मॉर्टिमर व्हीलर जैसे लोग यहाँ खाइयाँ काटते हुए धरती की परतें ऐसे पढ़ते गए जैसे दबा हुआ ग्रंथ।

panels.shot: close-up on Chandravalli Trader’s hands brushing away soil to reveal a silver coin emerging from the dark earth
panels.action: Chandravalli Trader leans close, breath held, as his fingers gently brush away moist soil from a small round glint of silver half-embedded in the trench wall.

dialogue.text: From the Satavahana levels came a surprise: tiny disks of distant empires—Roman denarii of Augustus, a Han coin, even a Roman bulla—that had slept in Deccan soil since the first centuries of our era.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन परतों से चौंक मिला: दूर साम्राज्यों के छोटे चांदी‑ताम्र चक्र—ऑगस्टस के रोमन दीनार, एक हान सिक्का, यहाँ तक कि रोमन बुला—जो युगों से दक्कन की मिट्टी में सोए थे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the Roman denarius obverse, faint imperial profile visible against the texture of age and soil grains
panels.action: The frame lingers on the worn face of Augustus on the silver coin, his profile faint yet distinct against pitted metal still flecked with clinging earth.

dialogue.text: On one coin, the profile of Augustus, first emperor of Rome; on another, the square script of Han China. Little worlds that had travelled by unseen hands to this inland basin.

i18n.hi: एक सिक्के पर रोम के प्रथम सम्राट ऑगस्टस की प्रोफ़ाइल; दूसरे पर हान चीन की चौकोर लिपि। छोटी‑छोटी दुनिया, जो अनदेखे हाथों से चलकर इस अंतर्देशीय घाटी तक आ पहुँचीं।

panels.shot: wide, cinematic view of an imagined Satavahana-era caravan moving through a Deccan forest track, low-angle from the ground
panels.action: In a past vision, Chandravalli Trader appears younger, walking beside a long caravan of pack bullocks and carts laden with jars and sacks, as they wind through a dense Deccan forest under towering trees.

dialogue.text: These coins did not drop from the sky. In the first centuries CE, when Satavahana rulers held the Deccan, caravans threaded forests like these, carrying pepper, textiles and stories along invisible trade veins.

i18n.hi: ये सिक्के आसमान से नहीं गिरे। जब पहली‑दूसरी सदी में सातवाहन दक्कन थामे थे, काफिले ऐसे ही जंगली रास्तों से मिर्च, वस्त्र और किस्से ढोते अदृश्य व्यापार‑नसों पर चलते थे।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Chandravalli Trader in the caravan, looking toward a distant Satavahana way-station by a tank
panels.action: From behind Chandravalli Trader, we see a modest Satavahana way-station by a shimmering tank: a few tiled-roof buildings, a simple shrine and men unloading goods under the watch of a local official.

dialogue.text: Chandravalli’s tanks and slopes offered what long-distance traders needed—water, shelter, a watchful eye of local power. Roman and Han coins here mark not tourists, but an older network reaching the Arabian Sea and beyond.

i18n.hi: चंद्रवल्ली के कुंड और ढलान लंबी यात्रा के सौदागरों को पानी, पनाह और स्थानीय ताकत की नज़र देते थे। यहाँ मिले रोमन‑हान सिक्के पर्यटकों के नहीं, उस पुराने जाल के निशान हैं जो अरबी सागर से आगे तक जाता था।

panels.shot: split-level shot showing archaeology trench at top and ghosted image of earlier megalithic stone circles below
panels.action: The panel layers time: at the top, Chandravalli Trader stands in the trench; below, faintly ghosted, stand ancient stone circles and cairns, suggesting burials from an even earlier megalithic age beneath him.

dialogue.text: Beneath the Satavahana coins lay older signs—a megalithic world of stone circles and cairns. Chandravalli had been a lived-in landscape long before Rome minted silver or Han officials cast bronze.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन सिक्कों के नीचे और पुरानी परत थी—मेगालिथिक पत्थर‑वृत्तों और ढेरों की दुनिया। रोम के चाँदी गढ़ने या हान के काँसा ढालने से बहुत पहले चंद्रवल्ली बसा‑बसाया भूभाग था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chandravalli Trader, now as a Kadamba-period figure, standing before the Chandravalli hill with an inscription rock in the foreground
panels.action: Time shifts; Chandravalli Trader, dressed in early Kadamba fashion, stands by a boulder bearing incised script, the Chandravalli hill rising behind and forest paths converging at his feet.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, another name appears on this landscape—the Kadamba Mayurasharma. His rock inscription near Chandravalli ties his emerging dynasty to this old nodal ground.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद इसी धरती पर एक और नाम उभरता है—कदंब मयूरशर्मा। चंद्रवल्ली के पास उसकी शिला‑लेखती उसकी उभरती वंशावली को इस पुराने नाड़ी‑केंद्र से जोड़ती है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of chisel poised on stone, with faint inscription lines already visible
panels.action: A craftsman’s steady hand holds a metal chisel against the rough face of the rock, fine grooves of fresh letters running alongside older, weathered lines.

dialogue.text: That inscription is brief, but it is a stake in stone. It says: this forest basin, once a Satavahana stop, now lies within Kadamba reach.

i18n.hi: लिपि छोटी है, पर पत्थर में गड़ा दावा है। उसका मर्म यह: यह वन‑घाटी, जो कभी सातवाहन पड़ाव थी, अब कदंब पकड़ में है।

panels.shot: wide, majestic shot of Banavasi townscape in the early Kadamba period, framed by river and fields
panels.action: Banavasi spreads along the Varada river—a modest town with tiled houses, a temple rising above, boats moored at the bank and distant paddy fields stretching to the horizon.

dialogue.text: From their capital at Banavasi, the Kadambas did not carve trade from empty rock. They stepped into a world where routes were old, but rulers changed.

i18n.hi: बनवासी की राजधानी से कदंबों ने शून्य चट्टान पर नया व्यापार नहीं تراशा। वे उन राहों पर उतरे जो पुरानी थीं, बस शासक नए थे।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a Kadamba court official handing a palm-leaf grant to a local landholder, with fields visible through an open doorway
panels.action: Chandravalli Trader, now as a Kadamba scribe, hands a rolled palm-leaf grant to a village headman, while outside the doorway farmers work new bunds along irrigated fields.

dialogue.text: Their innovation lay in how they used this inheritance—issuing agrarian grants, fixing rights over land and water, weaving peasant fields into the arteries that traders had long walked.

i18n.hi: उनकी नई चाल इस विरासत के इस्तेमाल में थी—खेती की दान‑भूमियाँ बाँटना, ज़मीन‑पानी पर हक तय करना, और किसानों के खेतों को उन धमनियों में पिरोना जिन पर व्यापारी बरसों चलते रहे थे।

panels.shot: close-up of a Kadamba copper coin on a wooden table, lion device clear, with faint Kannada legend around
panels.action: A Kadamba copper coin lies on a wooden table, a stylised lion standing proud at its centre, while around the rim faint Kannada letters arc like a new script asserting itself.

dialogue.text: Kadamba copper coins carried more than value. Some bore lions and early Kannada legends, quietly proclaiming a local language and symbol in a world used to others’ marks.

i18n.hi: कदंब ताम्र सिक्कों में महज़ कीमत नहीं थी। कई पर सिंह और आरंभिक कन्नड़ अक्षर थे, जो चुपचाप एक स्थानीय भाषा और चिन्ह को उस दुनिया में दर्ज कर रहे थे जो अब तक दूसरों की मुहरों की आदी थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chandravalli Trader examining a newly found 'Srimanaragi' coin with scholars around a table strewn with notes
panels.action: In a later, more modern setting, Chandravalli Trader sits with fellow scholars around a table, all leaning toward a small copper coin labelled in their notes, their faces thoughtful rather than triumphant.

dialogue.text: Recent finds, like a Banavasi coin tentatively read as ‘Srimanaragi’, excite debate. Yet careful voices insist: let evidence, not eagerness, decide what we can truly claim.

i18n.hi: नए खोजे, जैसे बनवासी का एक सिक्का जिसे संकोच से ‘श्रीमणारागि’ पढ़ा गया, बहस को चिंगारी देते हैं। पर सावधान आवाज़ें कहती हैं: दावा नहीं, सबूत तय करें कि सच में क्या कहा जा सकता है।

panels.shot: wide shot juxtaposing three coins on a dark cloth—Roman denarius, Han coin, Kadamba copper—lit by a single shaft of light
panels.action: On a dark cloth lit by a shaft of light, three coins lie in a neat row—a worn Roman denarius, a square Han coin with a central hole, and a Kadamba copper with lion and script.

dialogue.text: Laid side by side, the Roman silver, the Han bronze and the Kadamba copper do not tell of Kadambas trading directly with Rome or China. They tell of layered times along the same routes.

i18n.hi: रोमन चाँदी, हान काँसा और कदंब ताम्र को साथ रखो तो वे यह नहीं कहते कि कदंब सीधे रोम या चीन से सौदा करते थे; वे बताते हैं कि एक ही राहों पर समय की परतें चढ़ती गईं।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Chandravalli forest path today, with Chandravalli Trader walking contemplatively, holding a notebook
panels.action: In the present, Chandravalli Trader walks alone along a quiet forest path at Chandravalli, notebook in hand, the old tank glimmering through the trees and the rock with inscription just visible behind.

dialogue.text: The forest is quieter now. But every shard, every coin, every line of Mayurasharma’s stone reminds us: the Kadambas rose not from emptiness, but from an already humming landscape.

i18n.hi: जंगल आज शांत है। पर हर मर्तबान‑कसर, हर सिक्का, मयूरशर्मा की हर शिलालेख पंक्ति याद दिलाती है: कदंब शून्य से नहीं उठे, बल्कि पहले से गूँजती धरती से उगे।

panels.shot: slow push-in close on Chandravalli Trader’s thoughtful face as he looks at the coins in his palm, background fading into abstract maps and routes
panels.action: Chandravalli Trader gazes down at Roman, Han and Kadamba coins resting together in his palm, as behind him the forest fades into a faint overlay of trade routes and rivers drawn in light.

dialogue.text: Wise rulers, the Chandravalli story shows, do not boast of creating worlds alone. They read the old routes, respect their depth, and then quietly stamp them with a new, local name.

i18n.hi: चंद्रवल्ली की कहानी दिखाती है कि समझदार शासक दुनिया गढ़ने का घमंड नहीं करते; वे पुरानी राहें पढ़ते हैं, उनकी गहराई मानते हैं, और फिर उन पर चुपचाप अपनी स्थानीय मुहर जड़ देते हैं।
